criteria.evidence: Within this proposal's scope, the machine model is unchanged. Helpers remain ordinary materialised code under dialect §§12.1, 16 and 18; the delivery protocol adds no execution tier or primitive.

The operation list matches the runtime-backed rows of §§12.7–12.8 in both tracks. W>128 for ordinary arithmetic helpers and W>64 for multiplication-overflow helpers are correct. Arbitrary-width ctpop is also supported by the [LLVM 18 LangRef](https://releases.llvm.org/18.1.8/docs/LangRef.html#llvm-ctpop-intrinsic).

The diff preserves existing fault behavior, full-width count results, partial top limbs and slot ordering. Its non-emitting discovery explicitly preserves §12.1's rule order and repeated N22 applications. Requiring identical resolved bodies in both builds prevents comparison against a different implementation.

Major, triple and DataLayout are request-bound and checked. Ordinary helper rows retain §9.4's budget charges and §17.3's shadow-stack accounting. The note correctly acknowledges changed costs and dependent bindings without proposing an ISA ref@0.9 recipe change.

The delivery gap is real: §13.1 publishes an arith protocol, while §§12.7–12.8 and 19.1 provide no corresponding runtime-integer protocol. The proposed request canonicalisation, hashes and closure obligation repair it. JCS is an appropriate existing encoding ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html)). Generated-input provenance could be integrated more explicitly into the existing build record.
criteria.change: In the proposed §19.1 addition, state: "The §19.9 build record MUST identify each instance producer and version and record each canonical request hash and generated bitcode hash alongside the resolved base-runtime and arith hashes."

criteria.evidence: I reproduced successful LLVM 18/23 verification and both missing-definition assertions against the current runtime publications. Their hashes differ from INDEX's historical evidence pins, but the finding remains true. The arithmetic vector and INDEX's request digest also reproduce. The note correctly distinguishes these checks from execution of delivered helpers.
criteria.change: Under Conformance vectors, publish a tagged request fixture using INDEX's exact canonical bytes, with expected SHA-256 74e7a75be203bc350a18a84980258fa09a3e9936837e8aa67fb01532064cdd81, and a result fixture requiring product limbs [6,0,0,0,0], ctpop(product) limbs [2,0,0,0,0], and ctpop(a) limbs [3,0,0,0,0]. State: "Duplicate or reordered entries MUST reproduce this canonical request and digest."

criteria.evidence: The proposal preserves all admitted widths and treats missing generation as unfinished implementation, not a program fault. Its §19.1 addition and Mixed fat object section retain native host code, marked device closures, per-root certificates and closure-specific native comparison. The standing mixed-object check passes.
criteria.change: None required in the proposed diff.

criteria.evidence: The executable interface, completion semantics, dependency fixed point and restart rule are implementable. One small manifest ambiguity remains: 'every externally visible definition' includes LLVM data definitions, whereas function_type describes functions only. Function-only generated exports provide a straightforward conforming implementation.
criteria.change: In §12.8's OUTPUT_JSON paragraph, state: "For v1, exports inventories externally visible function definitions; generated implementation data has internal or private linkage, and shared runtime data is imported from the published base distribution." Alternatively add a tagged function/data export schema; I would use the function-only default.

suggestions: Proposed §19.1/build provenance: add "The §19.9 build record MUST identify each instance producer and version and record each canonical request hash and generated bitcode hash alongside the resolved base-runtime and arith hashes." This makes the note's repinning requirement directly actionable.

Proposed §12.8/OUTPUT_JSON: add "For v1, exports inventories externally visible function definitions; generated implementation data has internal or private linkage, and shared runtime data is imported from the published base distribution." A tagged function/data schema is also viable; prefer the simpler function-only default.

Conformance vectors: promote INDEX's canonical request into a tagged fixture with digest 74e7a75be203bc350a18a84980258fa09a3e9936837e8aa67fb01532064cdd81. Require reordered and duplicate entries to yield those same bytes. For a=2^256+3 and b=2, require product [6,0,0,0,0], ctpop(product) [2,0,0,0,0], and ctpop(a) [3,0,0,0,0].

Mixed fat object/shared background note: its certificate-table assertion that current text does not explicitly delimit native inventory is stale against current ISA §12.3 K85. Replace it with: "ISA §12.3 K85 already scopes fixed-image certificate inventory and native comparison to the selected marked closure; general container association and mixed-launch memory/lifetime bindings remain outstanding." This concerns the background note, not brt-vbi's delivery defect.
path_to_accept: No blocking changes are required. Apply through the recommended next 0.2 patch and corresponding 0.3 draft publication, preserving each track's ISA target; no ISA K entry is needed. To raise C6 from 4 to 5, promote the verified canonical request and arithmetic expectations into tagged normative fixtures.
summary: Accept. The delivery gap and missing i257 definitions are verified, the proposed fixed point preserves normalisation semantics, and mixed execution remains reachable. Hash consequences and the publication route are sound. Acceptance authorises the contract repair, not closure of brt-vbi/brt-zct implementation work.
